# Introduction

The Habitat Quality Monitoring Programme (MHQ) aims at the evaluation of biotic habitat quality of habitat types in Flanders.
The fieldwork data is collected by INBO and ANB.

For data management we created standerdized tables with information on the assessments, the measurements and the reference point.

The assessments table keeps track of:

+ assessment date of visited sampling units
+ accessibility of sampling units
+ whether the sampling unit is measured
+ observed vegetation type
+ relocation of sampling unit

The measurement table contains all measured sampling units and keeps track of

+ date of measurement
+ habitat type of measured sampling unit
+ the database reference to the actual fieldwork data

The reference point table contains information on the coordinates and the grts-ranking of the sampling units.
When a sampling unit is relocated, a new reference point is stored in the table.

These table are used to: 

+ track the progress of the monitoring programme
+ update the sample frame of the habitat types

In this document we will:

+ collect the administration data on new assessments and measurements in or before 2025
+ validate the new assessments and measurements (are they according to the field protocol)
+ update the standardized tables
+ evaluate the progress of MHQ

# Data sources

## MHQ terrestrial sample and relocation points for monitoring cycle 2

The MHQ sample for terrestrial habitat types in monitoring cycle 2 is stored as a git2Rdata file `mhq_terr_sample_c2` in the `mhq_terr_cycle2/output` folder of the [n2khab-mhq-design](https://github.com/inbo/n2khab-mhq-design) GitHub repository.
The folder also contains the potential relocation points (`mhq_terr_relocations_c2`).

```{r}
path <- fileman_up("n2khab-mhq-design")

mhq_terr_sample <- read_vc("mhq_terr_sample_c2",
                           file.path(path, "mhq_terr_cycle2/output"))

mhq_terr_relocations <- read_vc("mhq_terr_relocations_c2",
                           file.path(path, "mhq_terr_cycle2/output"))
```

## Standardised tables of mhq refpoints, assessments and measurements

The standardised tables are stored in the `data` folder of the [n2khab-sample-admin](https://github.com/inbo/n2khab-sample-admin) GitHub repository.

We use version 'rapportage2025', which contains assessments until and including the year 2024.

```{r}

path_mhq_terr <- "../../data/mhq_terr/rapportage2025"

mhq_terr_assessments <- read_vc("mhq_terr_assessments", 
                                root = path_mhq_terr)

mhq_terr_refpoints <- read_vc("mhq_terr_refpoints", 
                                root = path_mhq_terr) 
    
mhq_terr_measurements <- read_vc("mhq_terr_measurements", 
                                root = path_mhq_terr)

mhq_terr_popunits <- read_vc("mhq_terr_popunits", 
                                root = path_mhq_terr)
```

## Assessments and measurement INBO

### Assessments

The INBO fieldwork coordinator uses [this googlesheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1WkGPPYTb1Xytg5kJeOSxLvt3PUdFjlpPb4rwYG9znys/) to document which sampling units have been assessed.

In order to reproduce the workflow, we save a copy from the google sheet, dating 2026-08-24.
The file is saved in [this](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wFZINPaR137csS3q79l8hpGkX24eEAaG) google drive folder.
Copy the file to the folder 'data/admin_mhq_terr' in this R project.

```{r message = FALSE}

assessments_admin_inbo_orig <- read_csv2("../../data/admin_mhq_terr/voortgang_mhq_terrestrisch_2026.csv")

```

```{r}

assessments_admin_inbo <- assessments_admin_inbo_orig %>%
    select(-starts_with("...")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(assessment_date)) %>%
    mutate(db_ref_orig = db_ref,
           fieldwork_team = str_to_lower(fieldwork_team),
           assessment_date = as.Date(assessment_date, format = "%d-%m-%Y"),
           grts_ranking_draw = as.numeric(grts_ranking_draw),
        db_ref = ifelse(nchar(db_ref_orig) > 5 & str_detect(db_ref_orig, "_"), str_sub(db_ref_orig, end = str_locate(db_ref_orig, "_") - 1), db_ref_orig)
       ) %>%
    filter(fieldwork_team == "inbo" | is.na(fieldwork_team)) %>%
    mutate(type_observed = ifelse(point_code == "470546_1", "6230_ha", type_observed)) # CHANGE in admin table!

check_na <- assessments_admin_inbo %>%
    filter(is.na(lsvi_measurement))
#ok --> not measured yet

assessments_admin_inbo <- assessments_admin_inbo %>%
    filter(!is.na(lsvi_measurement))

year_min_cycle2 <- assessments_admin_inbo %>%
    filter(fieldwork_team == "inbo") %>%
    mutate(cycle = ifelse(is.na(reassessment_1), "c_1", "c_2"),
           cycle = ifelse(year(assessment_date) > 2022, "c_2", cycle)) %>%
    mutate(main_type = str_sub(type_target_all, 1, 4)) %>%
    group_by(main_type, cycle) %>%
    summarise(year_min = year(min(assessment_date)),
              year_max = year(max(assessment_date)),
              n_assess = n()) %>%
    ungroup()

```

### Measurements

The [INBOVEG database](https://inboveg.inbo.be/) contain the measurement data.

The MHQ data is exported from the INBOVEG database and stored as git2Rdata objects in the `processed/inboveg_mhq_terr` folder of the [n2khab-mhq-data] (https://github.com/inbo/n2khab-mhq-data) GitHub repository.
The export script can be found in the same repository (`src/export_from_inboveg/query_inboveg.rmd`).

We read following git2Rdata files:

+ `header_mhq_terr` (contains the reference point, measurement date, plot area, and the coordinates)
+ `classif_mhq_terr`(contains the observed habitat type)

In the MHQ sampling units vegetation composition is measured in a 3 m x 3 m plot and vegetation structure is measured in a 18 m radius circle plot.
In most cases, INBOVEG contains a separate record for the square plot and the circle plot.
The measurements in both plots can be matched to the sampling unit by the `user_reference` value.
The `user_reference` value is also used to link the measurements to the records in the INBO assessments table.

```{r}

path <- file.path(fileman_up("n2khab-mhq-data"), "processed/inboveg_mhq_terr")

header_mhq_terr <- read_vc(root = path, file = "header_mhq_terr") %>%
    mutate(assessment_date = as.Date(vague_date_begin))

classif_mhq_terr <- read_vc(root = path, file = "classif_mhq_terr") %>%
    select(-survey)

visits_mhq_terr <- header_mhq_terr %>%
    select(survey, user_reference, recording_givid, area, assessment_date, y = latitude, x = longitude) %>%
    left_join(classif_mhq_terr, by = "recording_givid") %>%
    select(-classif_key) %>%
    mutate(user_reference = ifelse(user_reference == "1474526_2", "1474526", user_reference), #Change in INBOVEG
           user_reference = ifelse(user_reference == "1346134_2", "1346134", user_reference), #Change in INBOVEG
           type_observed = ifelse(user_reference == "2541138" & is.na(type_observed), "7140_meso", type_observed),
           type_cover = ifelse(user_reference == "2541138" & is.na(type_cover), 100, type_cover)) %>% #Change in INBOVEG
    mutate(db_ref = str_to_lower(user_reference),
           db_ref = str_remove(db_ref, "double_"),
           db_ref = ifelse(str_detect(str_sub(db_ref, 1, 1), "[a-z]"), str_sub(db_ref, 1, 5), db_ref),
           db_ref = ifelse(nchar(db_ref) > 5 & str_detect(db_ref, "_"), str_sub(db_ref, end = str_locate(db_ref, "_") - 1), db_ref),
           db_ref = ifelse(str_sub(user_reference, 1, 2) == "BV", str_to_lower(user_reference), db_ref),
           year = year(assessment_date)
           )

check <- visits_mhq_terr %>%
    group_by(user_reference, area, assessment_date, type_observed, y , x) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)

visits_mhq_terr <- visits_mhq_terr %>%
    filter(!str_detect(user_reference, "double"))

check_missing_area <- visits_mhq_terr %>%
    filter(is.na(area))

check_missing_coord <- visits_mhq_terr %>%
    filter(x == 500 | y == 500)

visits_mhq_terr_wide <- visits_mhq_terr %>%
    mutate(cover_description = str_c(ifelse(is.na(type_cover), "?", type_cover), "% ", type_observed)) %>%
    mutate(plot_type = ifelse(area <= 9 | is.na(area), "square", "circle")) %>%
    mutate(plot_type = ifelse(recording_givid == "IV2025071010094321", "circle", plot_type)) %>% #!CHANGE IN INBOVEG  -> aangepast
    group_by(survey, db_ref, user_reference, recording_givid, plot_type, assessment_date, year, x, y) %>%
    summarise(cover_description = str_c(cover_description, collapse = "; ")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(31370)

check <- visits_mhq_terr_wide %>%
    group_by(db_ref, user_reference, assessment_date, plot_type) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)

check2 <- visits_mhq_terr_wide %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    group_by(db_ref, survey, assessment_date) %>%
    mutate(n = n_distinct(user_reference)) %>%
    filter(n > 1)

visits_mhq_terr_wide <- visits_mhq_terr_wide %>%
    mutate(x_measured = round(st_coordinates(visits_mhq_terr_wide)[,1], 2),
           y_measured = round(st_coordinates(visits_mhq_terr_wide)[,2], 2)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    mutate(recording_givid = str_c(plot_type, ": ", recording_givid)) %>%
    group_by(db_ref, user_reference, assessment_date, year) %>%
    mutate(recording_givid = str_c(recording_givid, collapse = "; "),
           x_measured = mean(x_measured),
           y_measured = mean(y_measured)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "plot_type", values_from = "cover_description") 

mhq_terr_measurements <- mhq_terr_measurements %>%
    mutate(assessment_date = measurement_date)

visits_mhq_terr_new <- visits_mhq_terr_wide %>%
    anti_join(mhq_terr_measurements, by = c("user_reference", "assessment_date")) %>%
    anti_join(mhq_terr_measurements, by = c("db_ref", "assessment_date")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(square))

check_unique <- visits_mhq_terr_new %>%
    group_by(assessment_date, db_ref) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)

check_na_square <- visits_mhq_terr_wide %>%
    filter(is.na(square)) %>%
    filter(str_detect(survey, "N2000"))

# 36790 square measurement zit in survey 'N2000_grasland_fieldapp_3' --> nog toevoegen aan measurements

```

## Assessments and measurement ANB

The assessment and measurement data of ANB is stored in a Fieldmap database.
The data is exported from this database and stored as git2Rdata files in the `processed/fieldmap_mhq` folder of the [n2khab-mhq-data] (https://github.com/inbo/n2khab-mhq-data) GitHub repository.
The export script can be found in the same repository (`src/export_from_fieldmap/query_fieldmap.rmd`).

Here we use the exported data from the `fieldmap_openhab version 2026-04-23` database, which can be found in this [Google Drive Folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FdWVd4rzSdriL5gyT1OCjxbXMc9PFPBY).

We read following git2Rdata files:

+ `assessments`
+ `coordinates`

The `coordinates` file is not stored in the repository as it is sensitive data.
We store the file in this [Google Drive Folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FdWVd4rzSdriL5gyT1OCjxbXMc9PFPBY).

```{r}

path <- file.path(fileman_up("n2khab-mhq-data"), "processed/fieldmap_mhq")

assessments_admin_anb <- read_vc(root = path, file = "assessments") 

type_observed <- read_vc(root = path, file = "type_observed") 

coordinates_anb <- read_vc(root = path, file = "coordinates")  

```

# Preprocessing: update assessments

Now we will identify new assessments compared to the 'rapportage2025' version.
We do this separately for INBO and ANB as data is organised in a different way.

## Assessments INBO

### Identify new assessments

A new assessment of a sampling unit can be detected by selecting new combinations of `assessment_date` and `point_code` in the INBO assessment table compared to the mhq_terr_assessments standardized table.

```{r}
assessments_table_old <- mhq_terr_assessments %>%
    mutate(grts_ranking_draw = as.numeric(str_sub(point_code, end = -3))) %>%
    left_join(mhq_terr_refpoints, by = "point_code") %>%
    mutate(year = year(assessment_date))

assessments_admin_inbo_new <- assessments_admin_inbo %>%
    mutate(year = year(assessment_date)) %>%
    anti_join(assessments_table_old, by = c("point_code", "assessment_date")) %>%
    left_join(select(assessments_table_old, point_code, year, x_exist = x, y_exist = y, assessment_date_exist = assessment_date), by = c("year", "point_code")) %>%
    mutate(dist = ((x_exist - x)^2 + (y_exist - y)^2)^0.5)

# here we check (unexpected) new assessments before 2025
check_new <- assessments_admin_inbo_new %>%
    filter(year < 2025)

```

We expect only new assessments from 2025.
Yet we also identify some new assessments older than 2025.

```{r}
check_new %>%
    select(point_code, assessment_date, db_ref, lsvi_measurement) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)
```

Explenation:

+ 1085366_1: selected for 2330_bu (ANB) and for 6230_hn (INBO); visited by ANB on 20-7-2017 and measured; visited by INBO on 31-7-2017 and not measured but replaced to 1085366_2; INBO assessment of 1085366_1 can be added

+ 1381569: similar situation as for 1085366

+ 50102: 50102_1 was visited twice in cycle 2, in 2019 and in 2022. 2019 assessment can be added.

+ 529473_1: to be added, probably missing due to wrong point_code in admin table (529473_2) --> corrected in admin table

+ 379222_1: to be added, probably missing due to wrong point_code (379222) --> corrected in admin table

Conclusion: all detected new assessments before 2025 can be added to the updated tables 

### Match new assessments with INBOVEG records

The measured sampling units are imported in INBOVEG.
For each sampling unit we create a database reference (`db_ref`)  based on which we can link the assessments and the measurements.

Here we will check that for all measured sampling units we find a record in INBOVEG.
Different cases can occur.

#### New assessments with a matching record in INBOVEG for the combination of `assessment_date` and `db_ref`

```{r}

assessments_measured <- assessments_admin_inbo_new %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    inner_join(visits_mhq_terr_new, by = c("db_ref", "year"), suffix = c("_admin", "_inboveg"))

check_date <- assessments_measured %>%
    filter(assessment_date_admin != assessment_date_inboveg)

assessments_measured <- assessments_admin_inbo_new %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    inner_join(visits_mhq_terr_new, by = c("db_ref", "assessment_date", "year"))
```

```{r}
assessments_measured %>%
    select(db_ref, assessment_date, type_observed, lsvi_measurement, recording_givid) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE,
              filter = "top")
```

#### New assessments but no matching measurement in INBOVEG

```{r, results='asis'}
assessments_measured_notinboveg <- assessments_admin_inbo_new %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    anti_join(visits_mhq_terr_wide, by = c("db_ref", "assessment_date")) 

```

`r if (nrow(assessments_measured_notinboveg) == 0) "Does not occur!"`

```{r, eval = nrow(assessments_measured_notinboveg) > 0}

assessments_measured_notinboveg %>%
    select(point_code, db_ref, assessment_date, lsvi_measurement, type_observed) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top")
```

#### New assessments that are not measured (and therefore no record in INBOVEG)

```{r}
assessments_not_measured <- assessments_admin_inbo_new %>%
    filter(!lsvi_measurement)
 
#check if there is no inboveg record
check <- assessments_not_measured %>%
    semi_join(visits_mhq_terr_wide, by = c("db_ref", "assessment_date"))
# ok: gaat om de originele locaties van verplaatste punten

```

`r if (nrow(check) > 0) "For following assessments without measurment, there is a INBOVEG record."`

```{r, eval = nrow(check) > 0}

check %>%
    select(point_code, db_ref, assessment_date, lsvi_measurement, type_target_all, type_observed) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)

```
Explanation:

Both assessments resulted in a relocation.
The measurements correspond with the relocated sampling units 1381569_2 and 1085366_2.

+   923346: assessment in 2025 is incorrect --> ignore
 
+   1474526: this assessment should be added in the admin table (for point_code 1474526_2)

```{r}
mhq_terr_assessments_update <- mhq_terr_assessments %>% #db_ref is missing
```

### Link assessments to the reference points of the sampling units

Next we link the new assessments to the reference points of the sampling units, to compare the assessed coordinates and the coordinates of the reference points.

```{r}

refpoints_assessed_inbo_new <- mhq_terr_refpoints %>%
    inner_join(assessments_admin_inboveg, by = "point_code") %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(distance = round(sqrt((x_measured - x)^2 + (y_measured - y)^2), 3))

check_missing_refpoint <- assessments_admin_inboveg %>%
    anti_join(refpoints_assessed_inbo_new, by = "point_code")

check_double_su <- refpoints_assessed_inbo_new %>%
    group_by(point_code, type_target_all, assessment_date) %>%
    mutate(n_pointcode = n()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(n_pointcode > 1)

```

+ First we check if the assessed sampling units occur in the sample for monitoring cycle 2

```{r}
check_su2 <- refpoints_assessed_inbo_new %>%
    # separate_wider_delim(point_code, delim = "_", names = c("point_code_base", "point_code_suffix"), cols_remove = FALSE) %>%
    filter(!point_code %in% mhq_terr_sample$point_code)
    # mutate(check_point_code_base = point_code_base %in% mhq_terr_sample$point_code_base) 

```

`r if (nrow(check_su2) == 0) {"All assessed sampling units occur in the sample"} else {"Following assessed sampling units are not part of the terrestrial sample cycle 2."}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_su2) > 0}

check_su2 %>%
    select(point_code, assessment_date, db_ref, type_target_all, type_observed, lsvi_measurement) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)

```

Explanation: these are assessments of monitoring cycle 1.

+ In the admin table the column `relocation` indicates if a sampling unit was relocated.
We check if this column is filled in for all measured sampling units.

```{r}
check_metadata <- refpoints_assessed_inbo_new %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    filter(is.na(relocation))
```

`r if (nrow(check_metadata) == 0) {"OK!"} else {"Complete records below!"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_metadata) > 0}
check_metadata %>%

refpoints_assessed_inbo_new <- refpoints_assessed_inbo_new %>%

```


`r if (nrow(check_coordinates) == 0) {"OK!"} else {"Check records below!"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_coordinates) > 0}
check_coordinates %>%
    select(point_code, db_ref, assessment_date, type_observed, x, y, x_measured, y_measured, distance, relocation, reassessment_1) %>%
```

## Assessments ANB

### Identify new assessments

We use `plot_id` in the Fieldmap database for `db_ref`

A new assessment of a sampling unit can be detected by selecting new combinations of `assessment_date` and `plot_id` in `assessments` git2Rdata file (exported from the Fieldmap database) compared to the mhq_terr_assessments standardized table.

```{r}
#waarom deze stap?: om een link te maken met de Fieldmap db
mhq_terr_assessments <- mhq_terr_assessments %>%
    mutate(db_ref = str_sub(point_code, end = -3))

coordinates_anb <- coordinates_anb %>%
    mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id))  

assessments_admin_anb_new <- assessments_admin_anb %>%
    mutate(db_ref = plot_id) %>%
    filter(type_target_all != "91E0_sf", #assessed by MONEOSINBO
           is.na(remark) | remark != "opname door INBO ikv verdroging") %>%
    rename(assessment_date = date_assessment) %>%
    anti_join(mhq_terr_assessments, by = c("db_ref", "assessment_date")) 

check_cycle <- assessments_admin_anb %>%
    mutate(main_type = str_sub(type_observed, 1, 4)) %>%
    group_by(main_type, mon_cycle) %>%
    summarise(year_min = min(year(date_assessment)),
              year_max = max(year(date_assessment)),
              n = n()) %>%
    ungroup()
```

The new assessments are shown in the table below.
The table also contains information on the presence of species cover records (square plot) and vegetation structure records (circle plot) in the database.  

```{r}
assessments_admin_anb_new %>%
    select(plot_id, assessment_date, info_status_fieldwork, type_target_all, type_observed, targethabitat, cover_species_record, structure_openhab_record) %>%
    arrange(assessment_date) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE,
              filter = "top")
```

### Link assessments to reference points

We link the new assessments to the reference points of the sampling units, to compare the assessed coordinates and the coordinates of the reference points.

```{r}
coordinates_anb_c2 <- coordinates_anb %>%
    filter(mon_cycle == 2) %>%
    select(point_code, x_measured, y_measured, mon_cycle, relocation = verlegd, grts_relocation = nr_vervangplot)

check_unique <- coordinates_anb_c2 %>%
    group_by(point_code) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)
# OK

assessments_anb_c2 <- assessments_admin_anb_new %>%
    filter(mon_cycle == 2) %>%
    rename(point_code = sampling_unit_code) %>%
    filter(remark != "opname door INBO ikv verdroging" | is.na(remark)) %>%
    left_join(coordinates_anb_c2, by = c("point_code", "mon_cycle"))
    
refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 <- mhq_terr_refpoints %>%
    inner_join(assessments_anb_c2, by = "point_code") %>%
    mutate(distance = round(sqrt((x_measured - x)^2 + (y_measured - y)^2), 3))

check_missing_refpoint <- assessments_anb_c2 %>%
    anti_join(refpoints_assessed_anb_c2, by = "point_code")
#OK
```

+ First we check if the assessed sampling units occur in the sample for monitoring cycle 2

```{r}
check_su2 <- refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 %>%
    filter(!point_code %in% mhq_terr_sample$point_code)

```

`r if (nrow(check_su2) == 0) {"All assessed sampling units occur in the sample"} else {"Following assessed sampling units are not part of the terrestrial sample cycle 2"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_su2) > 0}

check_su2 %>%
    select(point_code, assessment_date, db_ref, type_target_all, type_observed, lsvi_measurement) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)

```


+ n the Fieldmap database the column `verlegd` indicates if a sampling unit was relocated.
We check if this column is filled in for all measured sampling units.

We rename `verlegd` as `relocation`.

```{r}
check_metadata <- refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    filter(is.na(relocation))
```

`r if (nrow(check_metadata) == 0) {"OK!"} else {"The table below shows the records with missing data for relocation. We assume that relocation = FALSE when the distance between the measurement and the sampling unit is smaller than 1 m."}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_metadata) > 0}
check_metadata %>%
    select(point_code, assessment_date, lsvi_measurement, relocation, distance) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)

refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 <- refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 %>%
    mutate(relocation = ifelse(is.na(relocation) & (distance < 1), FALSE, relocation))
```

+ Check if there are assessments with relocation = FALSE but where the measured location is > 1 meter away from the reference point

```{r}

check_coordinates <- refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 %>%
    filter(distance >= 1, !relocation)

```

`r if (nrow(check_coordinates) == 0) {"OK!"} else {"Check records below!"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_coordinates) > 0}
check_coordinates %>%
    select(point_code, db_ref, assessment_date, type_observed, x, y, x_measured, y_measured, distance, relocation) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top")
```


## Combine assessments ANB and INBO

We combine the new assessments of ANB and INBO and do some quality checks.

```{r}

refpoints_assessed_all <- refpoints_assessed_inbo_new %>%
    mutate(not_measurable = NA,
           assessment_source = "field assessment") %>%
    bind_rows(refpoints_assessed_anb_c2 %>%
                   mutate(fieldwork_team = "anb",
                          survey = "anb_c2")) %>%
    select(survey, fieldwork_team, point_code, is_centroid, grts_ranking, type_target_all, type_observed, targethabitat, x, y, db_ref, assessment_source, assessment_date, inaccessible, not_measurable, lsvi_measurement, relocation, grts_relocation, x_measured, y_measured, user_reference, recording_givid, distance, remark) %>%
    arrange(grts_ranking) %>%
    mutate(type_target_all = ifelse(type_target_all == "2190", "2190_overig", type_target_all))
```

### Check observed habitat type

```{r}
types <- read_types()

has_subtypes <- types %>%
    group_by(main_type) %>%
    summarise(has_subtype = n() > 1 ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(has_subtype) %>%
    filter(main_type != "9120") %>%
    filter(!str_detect(main_type, "rbb"))

check_type <- refpoints_assessed_all %>%
    filter(is.na(type_observed) |
               (!type_observed %in% types$type)) %>%
   filter(!type_observed %in% c("gh", "onbekend"))

```

For the observed type we want to use a standardized list of codes:

+ the codes of existing habitat of RBB types in Flanders (`read_types()` of the n2khab  package)
+ `gh`: no habitat
+ `gdh`: no target habitat
+ `91xx`: any forest habitat type
+ `6xxx`: any grassland habitat type

We replace some of the categories used by ANB with the proper code, as shown in the table below.

```{r}
table_type <- data.frame(type_old = c("6 : (half) natuurlijke graslanden",
                                      "9 : bossen", "geen doelhabitat (meer)",
                                      "geen habitat (akker, houtkant, tuin,...)",
                                      "infrastructuur"),
                         type_new = c("6xxx", "91xx", "gdh", "gh", "gh"))

table_type %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)
```
Next we make following adjustments:

+ `type_target` = `4010` and `type_observed` = `4 : heide- en struikvegetaties` --> we assume that `type_observed` = `4010`
+ type_observed is missing:
    + we assume type_observed is `gdh` when `targethabitat` = `nee` (ANB) or `lsvi_measurement` = `FALSE` (INBO)
    + we assume type_observed is `onbekend` when `inaccisible` = `long term` or `not_measurable` = `long term`

The modifications are shown in the table below.

```{r}

table_type <- data.frame(type_old = c("6 : (half) natuurlijke graslanden",
                                      "9 : bossen", "geen doelhabitat (meer)",
                                      "geen habitat (akker, houtkant, tuin,...)",
                                      "infrastructuur"),
                         type_new = c("6xxx", "91xx", "gdh", "gh", "gh"))

refpoints_assessed_all_type <- refpoints_assessed_all %>%
    rename(type_old = type_observed) %>%
    left_join(table_type, by = "type_old") %>%
    mutate(type_new = ifelse((type_old == "4 : heide- en struikvegetaties") & lsvi_measurement, 
                                  type_target_all, 
                                  type_new),
           type_observed = ifelse(is.na(type_new), 
                                  type_old, 
                                  type_new),
           type_observed = ifelse(is.na(type_observed),
                                  ifelse(!is.na(inaccessible) | !is.na(not_measurable),
                                         "onbekend", 
                                         ifelse(!lsvi_measurement,
                                                "gdh",
                                                NA)),
                                  type_observed))

refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    semi_join(check_type, by = "point_code") %>%
    arrange(assessment_date) %>%
    select(point_code, assessment_date, type_target_all, type_old, type_observed, lsvi_measurement, inaccessible, not_measurable) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top")
```

Next we check if the subtype of the observed habitat type defined
If the observed subtype is not defined, we assume that the subtype corresponds with the target subtype.

```{r}
check_subtype <-  refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    filter(type_observed %in% has_subtypes$main_type)
```

`r if(nrow(check_subtype) == 0) {"OK: all subtypes are defined"} else {str_c("subtypes were added for ", nrow(check_subtype), " records")}`

```{r, eval = FALSE}

add_subtype_observed <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    filter(type_observed %in% has_subtypes$main_type) %>%
    separate(type_target_all, into = c("type_target_1", "type_target_2"), sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(type_observed = ifelse(str_sub(type_target_1, 1, 4) == type_observed, type_target_1,
                                  ifelse(str_sub(type_target_2, 1, 4) == type_observed & !is.na(type_target_2), type_target_2, type_observed))) %>%
    select(-type_target_1, -type_target_2)

refpoints_assessed_all_type <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    anti_join(add_subtype_observed, by = c("point_code", "assessment_date")) %>%
    bind_rows(add_subtype_observed)
```

### Check if the status is defined for all records

The status is defined when in any of following occasions:

+ `assessment_source` = `fieldwork assessment`
+ `inaccessible` = `long term` or `short term`
+ `not_measurable` = `long term` or `short term`

```{r}
# status of each survey event defined?
check_status <- refpoints_assessed_all %>%
    filter(is.na(assessment_source) & is.na(inaccessible) & is.na(not_measurable))

```
`r if(nrow(check_status) == 0) {"OK: status is defined for all records"} else {"Check following records, PLEASE!"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_status) > 0}
check_status %>%
    select(point_code, assessment_date, assessment_source, inaccessible, not_measurable) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE)
```

### Check if sampling units are assessed by both ANB and INBO 

If this is the case we select the assessment with a measurement.

```{r}
check_unique_point_code <- refpoints_assessed_all %>%
    mutate(year = year(assessment_date)) %>%
    group_by(point_code, year) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)

```
`r if(nrow(check_unique_point_code) == 0) {"OK: no sampling units are assessed both by ANB and INBO"} else {"Check following records"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_unique_point_code) > 0}

check_unique_point_code %>%
        datatable(rownames = FALSE)
    
refpoints_assessed_all_type <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    mutate(year = year(assessment_date)) %>%
    group_by(point_code, year) %>%
    filter(n() == 1 | (n() > 1 & lsvi_measurement)) %>%
    ungroup()
```

## Create new reference points for relocated population units

When a sampling unit is relocated, we have to define a new reference point (`point_code`).
Later we will check if the relocation is performed according to the protocol.

First we check the distance between the sample unit reference point and the measured coordinates.
When indicated that the assessment was not relocated, this distance should be smaller than 1 m (we allow a 1 meter location error). 

```{r}

refpoints_assessed_all_type <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    mutate(relocation = ifelse(is.na(relocation), FALSE, relocation))

check_no_replacement <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    filter(!relocation) %>%
    filter(distance > 1)
```

```{r}
refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = distance)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    facet_wrap(~str_c("relocation = ",relocation), scales = "free", ) +
    labs(x = "Aantal meetpunten")

```

Next we determine the `grts_ranking` of the new location and the distance to the nearest grid cell centre.
This distance should be smaller than 1 m.

```{r}

grts_master <- read_GRTSmh()

distance_from_centroidgrid <- function(min_x, min_y, measured_x, measured_y, resolution = 32, threshold = 1) {
    
    difference_x <- (measured_x - min_x) %% resolution
    shortest_distance_x <- min(difference_x, resolution - difference_x)
    difference_y <- (measured_y - min_y) %% resolution
    shortest_distance_y <- min(difference_y, resolution - difference_y)
    distance_from_grid <- sqrt( shortest_distance_x ^ 2 + shortest_distance_y ^ 2)
    
    return(distance_from_grid)
}

min_x <- (mhq_terr_refpoints %>%
    filter(is_centroid) %>%
    filter(x == min(x)))$x

min_y <- (mhq_terr_refpoints %>%
    filter(is_centroid) %>%
    filter(y == min(y)))$y

new_reference_points <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    filter(distance >= 1) %>%
    filter(lsvi_measurement) %>%
    group_by(point_code) %>%
    mutate(ranking_code = str_sub(point_code, end = -3),
           x_orig = x,
           y_orig = y,
           x = x_measured,
           y = y_measured,
           distance_centroid = distance_from_centroidgrid(min_x = min_x,
                              min_y = min_y,
                              measured_x = x_measured,
                              measured_y = y_measured),
           is_centroid = distance_centroid < 1,
           legacy_site = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 31370)

new_reference_points <- new_reference_points %>%
    mutate(grts_ranking = (terra::extract(grts_master,new_reference_points))$GRTSmaster_habitats) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() 
```

```{r}
check_relocation <- new_reference_points %>%
    filter(distance_centroid > 1)
```
`r if(nrow(check_relocation) == 0) {"OK: all relocations are within a distance of 1 m from a grid cell centroid"} else {"Check relocations below"}`

```{r, eval = nrow(check_relocation) > 0}

datatable(check_relocation,
              rownames = FALSE)

```

Finally we define a new point code for the relocated sampling unit as follows:

+ the point_code prefix (= `grts_ranking_draw`) of the original point_code is kept
+ a new point_code suffix is created by augmenting the maximum suffix value (for the point_code prefix) by one

We also check if the new point_code does not already exist.

```{r}

max_n <- mhq_terr_refpoints %>%
    select(point_code) %>%
    separate(col = point_code, into = c("left_part", "right_part"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(right_part = as.numeric(right_part)) %>%
    group_by(left_part) %>%
    mutate(max_n_point_code = max(right_part)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(point_code, max_n_point_code) %>%
    unique()

new_reference_points <- new_reference_points %>%
    left_join(max_n, by = "point_code") %>%
    mutate(x = x_measured,
           y = y_measured) %>%
    group_by(ranking_code) %>%
    mutate(n = n(),
           rank = rank(x),
           add = rank(x) + max_n_point_code,
           point_code_old = point_code,
          point_code = str_c(ranking_code, "_", add)
        ) %>%
    ungroup()

# check if new reference points already exist
check <- new_reference_points %>%
    semi_join(mhq_terr_refpoints, by = "point_code")

original_reference_points <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    semi_join(new_reference_points, by = c("point_code" = "point_code_old", "assessment_date")) %>%
    mutate(lsvi_measurement = FALSE,
           type_observed = "gdh", #geen doelhabitat
           distance = 0,
           x_measured = NA,
           y_measured = NA,
           user_reference = NA,
           recording_givid = NA,
           relocation = FALSE) %>%
    left_join(select(new_reference_points, point_code = point_code_old, relocated_to = point_code),
              by = "point_code")

check <- original_reference_points %>%
    group_by(point_code) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)

refpoints_assessed_all <- refpoints_assessed_all_type %>%
    anti_join(original_reference_points, by = c("point_code", "assessment_date")) %>%
    bind_rows(original_reference_points) %>%
    bind_rows(new_reference_points)

check_unique_point_code <- refpoints_assessed_all %>%
    group_by(point_code, assessment_date) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)

check_replaced <- refpoints_assessed_all %>%
    filter(relocation) %>%
    filter(str_detect(point_code, "_1"))

```
